title: Workplace Playbook: Essentials for Working at Redwood (2026)
author: Aisha Gomez
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook collects the core information every Redwood employee needs in their first 90 days and beyond: how we work, how roles and promotion work, key benefits and perks, a high-level hiring/onboarding overview, and the essential internal tools handbook. Treat this as a single-source operational reference — for detailed policies see the linked pages.

---

1) Working at Redwood — Principles and Routines

Core principles
- Developer-first mindset: prioritize productivity of engineers and ML teams when making tradeoffs.
- Production-first reliability: prefer safe, observable changes that preserve customer SLAs.
- Data minimization: default to least-privilege access for customer data and logs.
- Outcome-driven roadmaps: prioritize measurable impact over feature count.

Weekly cadence (typical team)
- Mon: 30m planning sync (asynchronous notes + short video optional).
- Tue–Thu: Deep work blocks (no recurring full-team meetings between 10:00–14:00 PT).
- Fri: 60m demo + retro alternating weekly with knowledge-share sessions.

Communication norms
- Slack: primary for fast operational communication. Use channels with clear prefixes: #eng-, #product-, #sre-, #ops-. Use threads for contextual discussions.
- Email: for external comms, contractual/financial items, and monthly all-company updates.
- Meetings: publish agenda and desired outcomes 24h prior. Prefer async updates when attendance would be >50% for informational items.

Working arrangements
- Remote-first: offices are hubs for collaboration; most teams are distributed.
- Core hours: optional, but teams may agree on a 4-hour daily overlap for real-time collaboration.
- Travel: reasonable travel for onboarding, critical syncs, and offsites is supported — request through Concur with manager pre‑approval.

---

2) Roles, Career Ladders, and Promotion Pathways

Leveling summary (high-level)
| Level | Typical titles | Ownership scope | Expected impact examples |
| L1 | Associate Engineer, IC I | Task-level, mentor support | Ship bugfix, write tests |
| L2 | Engineer, IC II | Feature-level ownership | Own a small feature, triage incidents |
| L3 | Senior Engineer, IC III | Cross-feature, technical leadership | Design subsystems, mentor juniors |
| L4 | Staff Engineer / Manager I | Service-level, team-wide influence | Lead architecture changes, manage teams |
| L5 | Senior Staff / Manager II | Multi-team influence, strategy | Define platform roadmap, lead cross-org projects |
| L6 | Principal / Director | Org-wide strategy | Drive company-level technical strategy |

Promotion criteria (process summary)
1. Candidate prepares promotion packet: updated resume, 3–5 signal projects, manager endorsement, self-evaluation aligned to rubric.
2. Calibration: hiring/leveling panel reviews packet against rubric across four core dimensions: technical craft, ownership & execution, mentorship & leadership, and impact & scope.
3. Decision: panel recommends promotion, defers with development plan, or rejects with feedback.
4. Timeline: typical cycle is quarterly; expedited promotions possible for exceptional contributions.

Examples of signals for promotion
- Technical craft: designed and executed a backwards-compatible runtime change that reduced median latency by 22%.
- Ownership & execution: owned a cross-team rollout with zero customer-facing incidents.
- Mentorship: regularly runs onboarding clinics and a documented apprenticeship plan.
- Impact & scope: influenced product roadmap that led to a measurable revenue/efficiency win.

Manager checklist for promotions
- Assemble packet and evidence.
- Run 1:1 calibration with peers and up-manager.
- Schedule leveling panel and notify people-ops.
- Deliver feedback to candidate regardless of outcome with a clear development checklist.

---

3) Benefits & Perks — Quick Reference

Health and financial benefits
- Medical, dental, and vision: US plans with multiple tiers; international equivalents supported via country benefits. Enrollment window: 30 days from start or annual open enrollment.
- 401(k) with company match: up to 4% match after 6 months.
- Equity: RSU grants for full-time employees on hire, periodic refreshes reviewed annually.

Time off and leaves
- PTO: flexible policy with manager-aligned coverage; recommended minimum notice for planned absences: 2 weeks.
- Parental leave: 16 weeks primary, 8 weeks secondary (paid). Additional support available via caregiver stipend.
- Sick leave: local statutory minimums apply, plus discretionary short-term disability top-ups in qualifying regions.

Learning & wellbeing
- Annual learning stipend: $1,000 USD (pro-rated first year) for courses, books, or conference attendance. Manager pre-approval required for >$250.
- Wellness allowance: $50/month stipend for mental/physical wellness.
- Home office: one-time setup allowance ($600) and monthly connectivity stipend ($50) for remote employees.

Family & inclusive benefits
- Adoption & fertility assistance reimbursement (policy and limits documented on benefits portal).
- Gender transition support and inclusive healthcare navigation resources.

How to use benefits
1. Visit the benefits portal (link pinned in #people-ops).
2. For urgent medical coverage questions, email benefits@redwood.ai and cc your people-ops partner.
3. For parental leave, start the process 90 days before planned leave when possible; manager and people-ops will coordinate coverage planning.

---

4) Hiring and Onboarding — Overview for Managers and New Hires

Hiring process (high-level)
1. Role request: hiring manager submits an approved headcount request with hiring rubric and salary band.
2. Sourcing & screening: TA sources candidates, conducts 30m screen focusing on role fit and core competencies.
3. Interview loop: typically includes work-sample exercise, technical interview, team fit, and hiring manager interview. Use the standard scorecard.
4. Offer & acceptance: comp approved by people-ops; offers run through the hiring committee for bands L4+.
5. Onboarding: once offer is accepted, the manager completes the New Hire Kickoff checklist in Workday and tools access requests.

Interview scorecard (core sections)
- Role-specific skills (1–5)
- System design / problem solving (1–5)
- Ownership & communication (1–5)
- Cultural fit & collaboration (1–5)
- Overall recommendation: Strong hire / Hire / Neutral / Do not hire

Onboarding checklist (first 90 days)
- Pre-onboard (HR & IT)
  1. Send welcome packet and manager 30–60–90 plan.
  2. Request access to essential systems (GitHub, Jira, internal slack).
  3. Schedule orientation and initial 1:1 slots.
- Day 0–1
  1. Complete benefits enrollment and payroll details.
  2. Hardware provisioning & VPN setup.
  3. Orientation: company mission, security basics, and team intro.
- Week 1
  1. Pair with buddy for product walkthrough.
  2. Complete first small ticket and write a short design note.
- Month 1
  1. Present a 15m demo of first deliverable.
  2. Schedule calibration with manager to set OKRs and success criteria.
- Quarter 1
  1. Deliver a scoped project and get feedback from three stakeholders.
  2. Review career development plan with manager.

Buddy program
- Every new hire gets a buddy (peer level or one level higher) for the first three months. Buddies are oriented via the Buddy Playbook and expected to provide weekly check-ins for the first month.

---

5) Internal Tools Guide — Essentials and Access Paths

Critical systems and primary owners
- GitHub (repos): owners - eng-platform. Use for code, PR reviews, and release automation.
- Jira (work tracking): owners - eng-platform + product. Boards are per squad; use issue templates for bugs, tasks, and incidents.
- Slack (communication): owners - eng-platform. #incidents channel owned by SRE.
- Confluence (docs): owners - people-ops. Document templates available in the top-level handbook folder.
- SSO & IAM (Okta): owners - security. All access requests flow through Okta groups.
- Monitoring & Logs (Grafana/Loki/Prometheus): owners - eng-sre. Alerts subscribe via PagerDuty.
- CI/CD (Buildkite): owners - eng-infra. Pipelines live in .buildkite/ and require CODEOWNERS approvals.

Access request flow (fast path)
1. Request access in Okta with the resource name and manager approval.
2. For repo-level access, open a GitHub access ticket in #infra-requests (use template).
3. For production system access, complete the elevated access form and an access review will be scheduled within 48 hours.

Command snippets and quick tips
- Git: git checkout -b feat/<ticket-number>-short-desc; open PR with link to Jira ticket.
- Jira short query: JQL: assignee = currentUser() AND statusCategory != Done ORDER BY priority DESC.
- Access escalation: if a required resource is blocking a new hire on Day 1 beyond 8 hours, ping @people-ops and @eng-platform with the ticket link for expedited handling.

Tooling best practices
- Keep docs updated: add a short README to any repo with >1 contributor.
- Use issue templates: triage will close non-compliant issues and request re-submission.
- Automate repetitive tasks: prefer a short script in infra/ rather than manual steps when >3 people follow a process.

---

6) Owner Contacts and Escalations

People-ops primary: people-ops@redwood.ai (response SLA: 24 business hours)
Security/Elevated access: security@redwood.ai (same-day for prod safety issues)
Eng platform: eng-platform@redwood.ai
SRE on-call: details in PagerDuty (link in Confluence)

Escalation quick guide
1. Blocker affecting customer production: page SRE on-call and post in #incidents.
2. Access block delaying onboarding beyond Day 1: escalate to people-ops and eng-platform on Slack and create a ticket.
3. Sensitive security incident: follow the Incident Response playbook and notify security@redwood.ai immediately.

---

Appendix: Templates and Links
- New hire 30-60-90 template: linked in the onboarding folder.
- Promotion packet template: linked in the leveling folder.
- Benefits portal, expense policy, and travel requests: links pinned in #people-ops.

If you have questions or suggestions for this playbook, file a Confluence edit request or ping people-ops in Slack.
summary: A concise, practical playbook for new and current Redwood employees consolidating work norms, career ladders, benefits highlights, hiring/onboarding steps, and essential internal tools guidance.
